subject: Throughput ladder, steady-state vs burst mapping + cross-connect checklist for private GPU pool
messages:
From: Sara Bishop <sara.bishop@acme-corp.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@example.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:17:00 -0800
Subject: Private pool sizing — sustained vs burst targets (Acme)

Vanessa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. To follow up with some concrete constraints from our side so you have the inputs for an initial sizing:

- Primary workload: live chat + semantic search. Typical request size ~ 350 tokens; embeddings/encodes at ~512 tokens for batch jobs.
- Steady-state SLA target: 95th pct response < 250ms for generation tail; supports ~650 QPS equivalent (requests that hit model).
- Burst patterns: marketing campaigns produce short spikes ~15–20m where concurrent QPS jumps to ~3,200, sustained up to 10 minutes. We need >90% of requests served with no fallback during these spikes.
- Persistence: KV cache warm-up window expected after deploys ~12–18 minutes; we'd like guidance on warm-pool buffer sizing.
- Networking: customer infra uses dual 10GbE cross-connects; we need a checklist to validate cable pinning, MTU, and egress shaping to avoid head-of-line stalls.

Can your team propose a throughput ladder (steady / near-peak / peak) with recommended node counts and warm-pool margins, plus a short cross-connect checklist we can run in our DC? Hoping to have a draft before next Tuesday's ops sync.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Bishop
Senior SRE, Acme Corp
[sara.bishop@acme-corp.com]

High-level plan:

- Jasmine to author a 1-page cross-connect + MTU + egress shaping checklist and recommended iperf/mtu test commands.
- I'll consolidate into a one-page ops handoff and include a warm-pool margin recommendation (baseline: 15% warm nodes + prioritized prefix caching for chat).

I'm attaching an initial throughput-ladder proposal (spreadsheet) and a short cross-connect checklist draft. These are sketches — Marissa will iterate.

Next step: Marissa, can you validate the numbers below and add a node-level estimate (GPU type assumptions: A100-80GB and 8-bit quantized M60 variants we often recommend for on-prem customers)? Jasmine, please add the checklist items you want me to push to Acme.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@example.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@example.com>, Sara Bishop <sara.bishop@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@example.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 14:18:43 -0800
Subject: Re: Private pool sizing — sustained vs burst targets (Acme)

Thanks all — did an initial pass on the ladder, sketching assumptions and node counts. Key points / numbers below (high level). See attached spreadsheet for full calc.

Assumptions (conservative):
- Avg tokens per request (generation): 350 tokens. Token throughput per A100-80GB for our tuned runtime at this sequence length: ~5,500 tokens/sec sustained (single model instance, non-multiplexed).
- Effective request throughput (350 tokens average) ~= 15.7 req/sec per A100 (5,500 / 350).
- For short-embedding batches (512 tokens), batching interop reduces effective per-GPU req/sec but increases token throughput — I'll include both dims in spreadsheet.

Sizing ladder (approx):
- Steady-state (650 QPS): ~42 A100s (650 / 15.7 = 41.4) -> recommend 48 nodes to give ~15% warm buffer and handling headroom for small infra jitter.
- Near-peak (3,200 QPS sustained 3–5m): ~204 A100s -> recommend enabling burst pool (mixed quantized M60s for cheap burst) with 220 nodes total in burst zone. Use autoscaler with 2-minute admission control and prioritized prefix cache to reduce tokens served during ingress spikes.
- Peak knee (extreme 10m campaigns): target headroom of additional 30% capacity via pre-warmed cold pool / queued admission + acceptable degraded-latency policy for background batch workloads.

Networking notes:
- Dual 10GbE cross-connects are borderline for sustained 3,200 QPS (model responses and embeddings egress). Recommend 25GbE if available. If not, ensure LAG across dual 10GbE with MTU 9000 and per-path shaping.
- Validate switch QinQ and jumbo frames end-to-end; packet drops at 0.1% produce long-tail latency issues for KV cache miss storms.

Operational recommendations:
- Warm-pool margin: 15% baseline; for predictable campaign windows move to 25% 1 hour prior to campaign start.
- Cache priming: provide a prioritized prefix list (top 10% of prompts) to seed KV cache.
- Admission control: 95th pct token-bucket threshold to start rejecting low-priority background jobs.

I'll update the spreadsheet with node-by-node math (A100 vs quantized M60 delta) and a short runbook for warm-pool choreography. Vanilla numbers above assume dedicated single-tenant pool; if you're multiplexing other low-latency tenants the margins shift upward.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@example.com

Vanessa/Marissa/Jasmine — this is excellent, thanks. A few quick clarifications and next actions from Acme ops: 

- We're on A100-80GB in our DC racks but can request a temporary 25GbE cross-connect upgrade for the campaign window if you recommend it. Please mark that as an action item in the one-pager.
- For the warm-pool choreography: can you include the preferred API call sequence and timing (example: set warm=TRUE -> pre-warm prefix list -> confirm KV hits > 70% before cutover)?
- We'll run the cross-connect checklist this week and share results (iperf logs / MTU test outputs) by Thursday.

If you can push the updated spreadsheet and the concise ops handoff by Wednesday EOD, we can lock validation on Thursday and schedule a brief 30-min dry-run next Monday.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — these numbers make it easier to budget the temporary cross-connect and pre-warm slots.

Best,
Sara
